problems.title: Undo a logarithm inside an exponent
problems.question: Evaluate $3^{2-\log_3 2}$.
problems.idea: Separate the subtraction in the exponent.
steps: The numerator is 3²=9.
The denominator is 3^(log₃2)=2.
The quotient is 9/2.

problems.title: Hexagonal-prism volume from a diagonal section
problems.question: A regular hexagonal prism has greatest diagonal-section area S. The distance between opposite lateral faces is h. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Express both given measurements using the hexagon side a and prism height H.
steps: The largest diagonal section is a rectangle with sides 2a,H, so S=2aH.
The face separation is h=a√3.
Then Sh=2√3a²H, whereas V=(3√3/2)a²H.
Therefore V=3Sh/4.

problems.title: Logarithms of powers of two
problems.question: Find log₃₂16.
problems.idea: Write the base and argument as powers of 2.
steps: Thus 5t=4 and the logarithm is 4/5.

problems.title: Detect a false logarithm identity
problems.question: All variables a,b,c,m,n,M,N exceed 2014. Which listed logarithm identity is false? One claims logₐb/logₐc=b/c.
problems.idea: Change of base gives a logarithm ratio, not an argument ratio.
formulas: Logarithm product, power and change-of-base identities apply to positive arguments and bases different from 1.
steps: Choose any a>2014, set c=a and b=a². Every variable used still meets the given bound.
The claimed left side is 2/1=2, but the right side is a²/a=a>2014.
This counterexample disproves the identity. The remaining listed equations follow from the usual logarithm rules.
problems.answer: The claim logₐb/logₐc=b/c is false (option ე).

problems.title: Count all real solutions of a periodic equation
problems.question: How many real solutions does 2^(sinx)+3·2^(-sinx)=4 have?
problems.idea: First solve for t=2^(sinx), then respect its limited range.
formulas: t+3/t=4 is equivalent to (t-1)(t-3)=0 for t>0.
steps: The roots for t are 1 and 3, but 3 exceeds the allowed maximum 2.
Thus t=1, which gives sinx=0.
All x=kπ, with integer k, work. There are infinitely many such inputs.

problems.title: A variable logarithm base excludes one candidate
problems.question: Solve logₓ(x²-2x+2)=1.
problems.idea: Impose the base conditions before converting the logarithm to an equation.
formulas: A real logarithm needs base x>0,x≠1, and positive argument.
logₓu=1 iff u=x on that domain.
steps: The argument (x-1)²+1 is always positive.
The equation becomes x²-2x+2=x, or (x-1)(x-2)=0.
The root x=1 is forbidden as a logarithm base. The root x=2 is valid.

problems.title: Volume from a slanted parallelogram base
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has base sides 4,6 enclosing 30°. Its lateral area is 30. Find the volume.
problems.idea: Find the prism height using the base perimeter, then use the parallelogram area.
steps: The perimeter is 2(4+6)=20, so the height is 30/20=3/2.
The base area is 4·6·sin30°=12.
The volume is 12·3/2=18.

problems.title: Locate a logarithm without a calculator
problems.question: Which listed interval contains log₀.₅20?
problems.idea: Bracket 20 between consecutive powers of 2.
steps: The bracket gives 4<log₂20<5.
Negating reverses the order: -5<log₀.₅20<-4.
Therefore the logarithm belongs to the listed closed interval [-5,-4].

problems.title: A power inequality with a base below one
problems.question: Solve $(\log_{30}16)^{\sqrt{x^2+1}}<2\log_{30}4$.
problems.idea: The right side equals the same base to the first power.
steps: Put A=log₃₀16. Since 1<16<30, 0<A<1.
The inequality becomes √(x²+1)>1.
Squaring nonnegative sides gives x²>0, hence x≠0. At zero equality holds and is excluded.

problems.title: A right triangular prism with equal base and lateral areas
problems.question: A right prism has an isosceles right-triangle base with equal legs 4. Its lateral area equals its base area. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Compute base area and perimeter to obtain the prism height.
steps: The base area is 4·4/2=8 and the hypotenuse is 4√2.
The perimeter is 8+4√2. Thus the height is 8/(8+4√2)=2-√2.
Multiply by the base area to get V=8(2-√2).

problems.title: Express a reciprocal logarithm through two given values
problems.question: If log₃2=a and log₃5=b, express log₁₀3.
problems.idea: First form log₃10, then invert it.
steps: Because 10=2·5, log₃10=a+b.
The requested logarithm reverses the base and argument.
Hence log₁₀3=1/(a+b).

problems.title: A radical exponent and a reciprocal base
problems.question: Solve $(\log_5 2)^{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\le(\log_2 5)^x$.
problems.idea: Use reciprocal logarithms and the decreasing exponential base.
steps: The radical requires x≤-1 or x≥1.
With A=log₅2∈(0,1), the inequality is A^(√(x²-1))≤A^(-x), so √(x²-1)≥-x.
For x≥1 the left side is nonnegative while -x is negative, so it holds.
For x≤-1, -x=|x| but √(x²-1)<|x|, so it fails.

problems.title: Minimum of a logarithm with base less than one
problems.question: Find the minimum of y=log₀.₂₅(4-x²).
problems.idea: A decreasing logarithm is smallest where its positive argument is largest.
formulas: For 0<b<1, log_b t decreases as t increases.
steps: On the domain, 4-x²≤4, with equality at x=0.
Thus the minimum is log₁/₄4.
Because (1/4)^(-1)=4, that value is -1.

problems.title: A cancelled logarithm still restricts the graph
problems.question: f(x)=x²-x-2. Which graph represents g(x)=5^(log₅f(x))?
problems.idea: The algebraic cancellation works only where the logarithm exists.
steps: The domain requires f(x)>0, giving x<-1 or x>2.
On those two intervals, g(x)=x²-x-2.
The graph contains only the two positive outer branches of the parabola. There is no middle arc or horizontal segment.
The points at x=-1 and x=2 are excluded because the logarithm of zero is undefined.
problems.answer: The two separated outer branches (option ვ, bottom right).

problems.title: Volume from three box face areas
problems.question: A rectangular box has three different face areas S1,S2,S3. Express its volume.
problems.idea: Their product is the square of the volume.
formulas: If edges are a,b,c, then S1=ab,S2=ac,S3=bc.
steps: Multiply the three areas to get (abc)².
The volume is abc>0.
Take the positive square root, giving V=√(S1S2S3).

problems.title: Cube volume from a space diagonal
problems.question: A cube’s space diagonal is d. Express its volume.
problems.idea: The space diagonal is √3 times the edge.
steps: The edge length is a=d/√3.
Cube it: V=d³/(√3)³.

problems.title: A logarithm identity rules out every solution
problems.question: Solve logₓ(x²)=6.
problems.idea: For every valid base x, the left side is always 2.
steps: On the allowed domain, logₓ(x²)=2.
The equation would require 2=6, which is impossible.
The tempting value x=1 cannot be used as a logarithm base.

problems.title: Midpoint distance as a fraction of a cube edge
problems.question: In a cube, M is the midpoint of A1B1 and N of AD. Find MN divided by the edge length.
problems.idea: Use a unit cube because the desired ratio is unchanged by scaling.
steps: MN²=1/4+1/4+1=3/2, so MN=√6/2 for unit edge.

problems.title: An exponential cannot take the same value twice
problems.question: For which a does 3ˣ=a have two real solutions?
problems.idea: The function 3ˣ is strictly increasing.
formulas: For base b>1, bˣ is strictly increasing and positive.
steps: For a>0 the equation has exactly one solution, x=log₃a.
For a≤0 it has none, since 3ˣ is always positive.
Neither case gives two solutions.

problems.title: Possible diagonal-to-side ratio in a square prism
problems.question: Which listed value can be a regular square prism’s space diagonal divided by base side: 0.3,0.4,0.5,0.7,1.4,1.6?
problems.idea: The two horizontal diagonal components already give a strict lower bound √2.
formulas: For base side a>0 and height h>0, d²=2a²+h².
steps: All listed values up to 1.4 are below √2, so they cannot occur.
For d/a=1.6, the required height ratio satisfies (h/a)²=1.6²-2=0.56>0.
A positive height exists, so 1.6 is attainable.

problems.title: Order powers by their bases and exponent signs
problems.question: Order x=0.2^(log₂9), y=1.5 raised to the positive power 2^(-log₀.₂3), and z=1 increasingly.
problems.idea: Only whether each value lies below or above one matters.
formulas: For A>1 and t>0, Aᵗ>1; 2ᵘ>0 for every real u.
steps: log₂9>0, so x lies strictly between 0 and 1.
The exponent 2^(-log₀.₂3) is positive. Since 1.5>1, y>1.
Thus x<z<y.

problems.title: Diagonal inclination from two lateral-face angles
problems.question: A box diagonal makes angles α,β with the two lateral-face directions. cosα=5/6 and cosβ=2/3. Find its angle θ with the base.
problems.idea: The squared perpendicular components to the three coordinate planes sum to the diagonal length squared.
formulas: For diagonal length d and components a,b,h: a²+b²+h²=d².
steps: The inclination is acute, so sinθ=√5/6.

problems.title: Triangle formed by axis intercepts
problems.question: Find the area of the triangle formed by the axis intercepts of y=-3^(x²-1)+27.
problems.idea: Solve for the two horizontal intercepts and use the vertical intercept as the height.
formulas: For base 3, equal powers have equal exponents.
steps: At y=0, 3^(x²-1)=27=3³, so x²=4 and x=±2.
The horizontal base has length 4.
problems.note: None of the listed answer values equals 160/3. The exponent in the source includes the subtraction by 1, which makes the y-intercept 80/3.

problems.title: Prism vertices from space-diagonal count
problems.question: A prism has 54 space diagonals. Find its number of vertices.
problems.idea: Count diagonals joining vertices on opposite bases but not contained in a face.
formulas: An n-gonal prism has n(n-3) space diagonals and 2n vertices.
steps: For each bottom vertex, three top vertices are joined by edges or face diagonals; the other n-3 give space diagonals.
The positive side count is n=9, giving 18 vertices.

problems.title: Distance from the upper centre to a lower vertex
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has base side a and height b. Find the distance from the upper base centre to a lower base vertex.
problems.idea: The perpendicular projection is the lower base centre.
steps: The horizontal separation from a base centre to a vertex is a/√3.
The vertical separation is b, perpendicular to the base.
The requested distance is √(b²+a²/3).
